newsitem.title: JAPAN: Showa Shell stops issuing wholesale price details.
newsitem.headline: Showa Shell stops issuing wholesale price details.

text.p: Showa Shell Sekiyu KK said on Wednesday that it has decided to stop disclosing information on its wholesale oil product prices from July.
"We've decided not to release any information (on prices)," a company spokesman said.
He said the company believes there is little value in announcing information on wholesale prices because of the wide disparity in wholesale and retail prices.
"The (retail) market no longer reflects wholesale prices...(releasing information) has lost its meaning," the spokesman said.
Many Japanese refiners introduced a new wholesale pricing system in April 1996 when oil product imports were liberalised, in an attempt to combat imports and make oil product trade more transparent.
These refiners release wholesale prices of gasoline, gas oil and kerosene every month based on foreign exchange fluctuations and crude oil prices.
Showa Shell, which is owned 50 percent by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, had not been revealing its wholesale price but had been announcing the margin of change in its monthly prices.

Japan's average gasoline and gas oil prices at the pump stood at 104 yen and 82 yen per litre, respectively, as of June 10, both down one yen from the previous month, an energy research body said on Monday.
A fierce price war at the pumps has sharply eroded the profit margins of oil companies.
